name: Titoism
description: A Yugoslav socialist tradition combining social ownership, worker self-management, federalism and international non-alignment.

axes.brief: Delegates, worker participation, recall and responsibility coexist with the League of Communists’ leading role.
axes.counterEvidence: Doctrinal replaceability and self-government differ from Tito’s personal lifelong presidency; socialist competition is not unrestricted multi-party alternation.

axes.brief: Declared personal rights and self-management operate within protection of the socialist order.
axes.counterEvidence: Actual suppression of dissidents qualifies constitutional liberty promises; doctrine and historical enforcement are both retained.

qualifications.10: Private communication rights and defence of the socialist order compete.

axes.brief: Equal nationalities and languages are constitutive parts of brotherhood and unity.
axes.counterEvidence: Shared socialist cooperation limits claims that every separate custom overrides equality or common institutions.

qualifications.9: Common practical schedules and distinct national calendars coexist.

axes.brief: International worker solidarity and non-aligned openness favour mobility and protection without cultural hierarchy.
axes.counterEvidence: Exact visas and settlement procedures are contextual extensions; collective economic capacity still constrains administration.

axes.brief: Peaceful coexistence, general people’s defence and disarmament accompany support for national liberation.
axes.counterEvidence: Anti-colonial solidarity permits some force beyond the narrow defensive-only wording; non-alignment is not pacifism.

axes.brief: Independent development rejects bloc domination while favouring international cooperation and negotiated rules.
axes.counterEvidence: Non-alignment rejects compulsory common foreign policy, not all collective action or accepted international obligations.

axes.brief: Social ownership with worker control replaces capitalist private ownership of major production.
axes.counterEvidence: Public is the bank’s closer collective category; social ownership must not be described as universal central state administration. Personal possessions and limited private activity remain.

axes.brief: Socially owned enterprises trade internationally and can cooperate with foreign producers under social priorities.
axes.counterEvidence: Strategic ownership and development protection qualify completely equal uncontrolled foreign acquisition.

qualifications.11: Reciprocity and peaceful open exchange compete.

axes.brief: Associated workers decide enterprise activity within negotiated social development plans.
axes.counterEvidence: The 1970s strengthened coordinated planning; neither pure command allocation nor unrestricted private markets captures the doctrine.

axes.brief: Solidarity, equal opportunity and regional development accompany entitlement to the fruits of labour.
axes.counterEvidence: Enterprise earnings differences and individual material incentives qualify complete equalisation of every income.

axes.brief: Civil socialist authority and private religious freedom replace religious foundations of national government.
axes.counterEvidence: Constitutional worship protections do not make religious doctrine an official legislative source; historical accommodation remains possible.

axes.brief: Social emancipation and equal participation favour changing inherited hierarchies.
axes.counterEvidence: Constitutional equality does not explicitly settle every contemporary sexual-identity curriculum or inherited custom.

qualifications.6: Family support and freedom from compulsory family roles coexist.
qualifications.16: National cultural inheritance and socialist transformation compete.

axes.brief: Developing productive forces is explicit, with collective responsibility for public safety and resources.
axes.counterEvidence: Modern gene editing and implants are analogies to productive scientific development; long-term harm remains a constraint.

axes.brief: Federal national autonomy and municipal self-management coexist with solidarity and nationwide coordination.
axes.counterEvidence: Constitutional self-determination includes secession while preserving mutual duties; practice often suppressed separatist mobilisation.

axes.brief: Social institutions and associated work are treated as transformable causes of conduct and opportunity.
axes.counterEvidence: Biological individuality need not be denied; exact temperament mechanisms are less specified than rejection of racial hierarchy.

qualifications.12: Personal variation and social formation compete.

phrase: A society where workers manage socially owned production and diverse national communities cooperate in an independent socialist federation.

religion.reason: The doctrine imposes no faith prerequisite; constitutional civil authority and private worship are distinguished.
